notes.title: Discord Q&A Stream Highlights!
notes.content:
[h2]Hola Capos! 

Recently we conducted a Q&A Livestream on our Discord, and here are the highlights! [/h2]

[h3]Unfortunately, the video footage from the stream was corrupted, so it became our first podcast! Enjoy! ːcartel_roflmaoː[/h3]

[previewyoutube=RFaX5wjoDd8;full][/previewyoutube]

Text version:
[expand type=details]

[olist]
[*] [b]How long did it take to make San Rafaela?[/b] We started working on San Rafaela almost 1.5 years ago! We actually found one of the first map drafts to show you! The goal of this map was to challenge not only the new players but the experts of our first map as well! We also wanted the map to look different from the first one, so we modeled new city buildings, new plants, trees, biomes, and water. So, yeah, we started thinking about San Rafaela even earlier but started making it 1.5 years ago.
[*] [b]Is Andrey a programmer?[/b] Nope, I’m just a community manager, but I’m learning a lot from my awesome colleagues! I’ll answer another question cause that was a pretty short answer! 
[*] [b]I’m terrible at the game, can you teach me?[/b] All I can tell you is that I have over 300 hours in the game, and I sometimes feel like I’m playing for the first time. Trial and error are the best teachers in Cartel Tycoon! But with recent updates, we were closely looking for feedback from players who are just starting out - we wanted to make the game easier to get into, to make these first hours feel good for the player. So, if you’re having trouble with the game - tell us what systems aren’t explained enough, and we’ll take a look at them! In the meantime, you can talk to awesome players on this server, who, I feel like, sometimes know the game better than us.
[*] [b]How was it working with tinyBuild? Any interesting stories?[/b] It’s great! They supported us from the beginning, and we couldn't have made this game without them! As for interesting stories, we can show you the first teaser draft that we pitched the game with! Back then there were only five people on the team, and we all pitched in to make this teaser that started our journey with tinyBuild and Cartel Tycoon. It’s an exclusive, don’t show anyone else!
[*] [b]How is the art for this game made? It’s incredible![/b] We agree it’s completely incredible! We have two 2D artists and four 3D artists! 2D artists are responsible for the UI and character designs and cinematics, while 3D artists are responsible for all of the 3D in the game - cars, trees, birds, buildings, the whole map! Our 2D  character artist uses the IPad and Procreate as her main tools of trade, and for 3D we use 3DS Max and Blender! We will tell our artists that you love their work! A lot of work-in-progress visuals, early concepts, ideas, cinematics storyboards, and many more can be found in our official artbook. Oh, and as a bonus, I’ll show you early sketches of some of the cinematics!. For each character, there’s always a mood board reference board with all the ideas and elements that we’d like to incorporate. Each character has its own backstory that’s tightly connected with how it looks. So, it’s always a collaboration between artists, game designers, and writers. 
[*] [b]We also had a lot of questions about the future of Cartel Tycoon.[/b] So we’re going to try to answer all of them at once. After the release of San Rafaela and multiple free updates for the game, we want to take a break from constant releases and focus on our long-term plans for the game - researching mod support, for example. We will, of course, continue releasing patches with bug fixes and small changes if needed. The next patch should be released in 2 weeks and will not only contain bug fixes but also some changes based on the feedback we got on Discord and from Steam reviews. But no big content drops are planned until the end of 2023. 

We’re also taking a step back to look through all of the feedback provided to us and to calculate which requested features can be added to the game and which of the features require a new game of their own! For example, auto-buying from Area Depots and Villages. Next year Cartel Tycoon is also releasing on consoles, so we need to focus on helping and supporting the porting team to get the best version of Cartel Tycoon possible! We don’t have a concrete release date for the console edition yet, but we’re hoping for a spring release. 

Another reason we’re slowing with the updates is that… we have new projects in development! We won’t share any details just yet but just wanted to let you know we’re cooking something up unrelated to Cartel Tycoon! 

[*] [b]There were also a couple of questions about future DLCs.[/b] Right now, we don’t have plans for future DLCs, but we’re also juggling a couple of long-term ideas and are thinking of different ways of implementing them! We also don’t want to simply release a DLC with new characters without providing a free update for all of the Cartel Tycoon owners, and as we said above - we’re focusing on the long-term plans and ideas, so if we find an idea that warrants creating several new characters while also providing awesome content for all of the Cartel Tycoon owners - we’ll make a small DLC!
[/olist] 

So, to sum it all up - we have plans for the long-term future of Cartel Tycoon, but we need to take a breather to focus on them fully. We’ve been releasing an update a month (well, almost) for 2 years now, so with the latest huge release behind our backs, we finally feel like the game is in a healthy position where we’re able to do that. It doesn’t mean that it can’t be improved further, no! We’re still taking your feedback to heart, and, in fact, pretty soon we should be adding one of the most requested features into the game!

We wanted to thank you for being with us through these eventful years and helping us make the game that we always wanted to make. And making it better along the way! We always try to thank you, and we’ll continue doing so! 
[/expand]

[*] [url=https://www.facebook.com/CartelTycoon/]Facebook[/url]

notes.title: San Rafaela is almost here... - Devlog 27
notes.content:
[h2]Hola Capos![/h2] 

[h3]San Rafaela DLC is launching this Friday! We made a devlog to talk about the features coming with this DLC![/h3]

[previewyoutube=d4DxUuk6ESE;full][/previewyoutube]

[h3]Devlog script: [/h3]
[expand type=details]Hola Capos! 

Hola Capos! My name is Andrey, the community manager of Cartel Tycoon, and today I’m here to tell you about the biggest DLC in Cartel Tycoon history… San Rafaela! Got your bags, got your sunscreen? Then, let’s get right to it! 

San Rafaela DLC is coming on September 22, and you can wishlist it on Steam right now! The DLC not only brings a new map but also a new campaign, new and returning characters, new mechanics, fresh challenges, and new means to overcome them! And new music! Let’s talk about all of them! 

First up, new map. San Rafaela is bigger than the Republic of De Ojeda, our original map, but don’t let that fool you - treacherous terrain like deserts and swamps will require you to adapt your production lines and reconstruct (pun intended) your operation in a new way. We wanted the map layout to feel fresh and offer a challenge even to those who already feel completely comfortable on De Ojeda. The roads between cities became longer, and a timely place police cordon can disrupt your operations. But you have a new Ace in your sleeve… 

Ferry Stations! Ferry Stations allow water traversal for your Lieutenants and production trucks! Your Smuggling Point is getting too much attention from the Police? Just capture a Ferry Station in a different region! Need to deliver goods to a Special Building but Enemy Region is blocking the path? Ferry Stations will help you out! Want to attack the enemy on the other side of the coast? Load your Ferries with weapons and Lieutenants, and send them on their merry way! 

One thing we’ve been relatively silent about is the new campaign. And that’s because we didn’t want to spoil it! The campaign is called ‘Crashing the System’, and it sends your Capo on a completely new path we haven’t explored in previous storylines… a political path. You see, you can’t buy everything in San Rafaela with dirty cash and a couple of guns - you need influence, and that’s what your Capo wants! As always, the outcome of the campaign depends on your choices and tactics. Get ready to meet new and familiar characters, some of which help you on your journey while others will try to put you in the ground.

The winners of the recent contest held in our Discord will also find that their submitted texts will be incorporated into the campaign! Congrats to them again! 

Along with the DLC, we’ll be releasing a Balance Update that will be available to everyone - We’ve heard your feedback On Discord, in reviews, and from the playtests, so we’ll be bringing changes to Laundering mechanics, combat, and Terror gain! 

Once again, the San Rafaela DLC will be released on September 22. The DLC will be available for 14.99 (Regional prices may vary) as a standalone or in a new anniversary bundle which will include all of the additional content released for Cartel Tycoon before and the San Rafaela DLC. Add it to your wishlists on Steam to not miss the release date, and tell us in the comments to what part of the DLC you’re looking forward to the most! 

Don’t forget to like, subscribe, and join our Discord to talk with the developers and other fans of the game! See you on September 22, Capos! Bye-bye!
[/expand]

notes.content:
[h2]Hola Capos![/h2]

Balance tweaks to Terror and Combat duration are aimed to lessen the pressure on the player but to keep this part of the game engaging.

notes.title: Anniversary Update // Devlog + Patch Notes
notes.content:
[h2]Hola Capos![/h2] 

[h3]We want to celebrate the one year anniversary of Cartel Tycoon leaving Early Access with an [b]Anniversary Update[/b] and some goodies for all of you![/h3]

[previewyoutube=4f49PNsC35k;full][/previewyoutube]

[h3]Devlog script: [/h3]
[expand type=details]Hola Capos! 

My name is Andrey, and I’m the community manager of Cartel Tycoon. We have a huge date this week - July 26 will mark one year since the 1,0 Release. Since then, we have had a lot of updates: we introduced multiple new mechanics, balanced existing ones, made new Lieutenants, and, of course, listened closely to your feedback.

We want to celebrate one year anniversary of Cartel Tycoon leaving Early Access with an update and with some goodies for all of you! Let’s get right into it! If you’re watching this before July 28, you can playtest the San Rafaela map on Steam! Leave a like on this video if you want a vacation there… 

So, it’s been one year since we left Early Access. Since then, we’ve published four major updates to the game and are working on another one right now, not including the San Rafaela DLC. The update we’re publishing today is a tad smaller, but it is still very important because we’ve wanted to focus on your feedback. 

First off, optimization. It’s been quite some time since we optimized the game, so we wanted to push the optimization further with this update. In particular, we’ve focused on the late game. Some of you know that when you build A LOT of buildings, the FPS takes a major hit. Or used to take it. Now, where you used to get 18 fps, you can get 50! Our internal tests were very promising, so we hope that you’ll feel these changes and they will lead to a much more comfortable experience! 

Secondly, balance. The introduction of the Combat System, in some cases, made the game harder than we expected, especially for new players, so we wanted to address the issue with this update further. Firstly, we wanted to address Terror and the situations when defending your building from an Enemy Gang would lead to activating the Attention Star, and defending your building from the Police would activate another, and you would be stuck in the loop of everyone constantly attacking you. Now, fights in buildings generate Terror at a much slower rate. 


Another issue with Terror was Guerrillas and Allied Gangs generating it for you even if your LTs left the fight leading to cases when your allies were responsible for your downfall. In this update, Guerrillas and Allied Gangs will leave the encounter if there are no player Liutenants in the fight AND if their Power is lower than the Power of your Enemy. We’ve also made Guerrilla convoys stronger - they now have 8 power instead of 5.

 
We’ve also upped the Allegiance of Enemy Gangs at the start of the game, so they won’t start to attack you when you’re just building your first production chain.


Another thing we’ve changed with the update is the Evacuation. Now, if you decide to leave your injured Lieutenant in the fight, you’ll be able to evacuate them for free after the fight ends - a reward for taking a risk! 


We’ve also changed Area Depots. This building used to be very powerful from the get-go, so we initially nerfed it a bit but also added it to the Research Tree so that you can upgrade as your Empire and your needs grow! 

There are smaller changes and, of course, bug fixes in the update, and you can read the full list in the Patch Notes that will be published with the update! 

Another thing we’ve added with the update are shine new Anniversary Emblems for your Cartel! You can select them at the start of your run, and they are available to everyone! 


After this release, we’ll be taking a small break in August - we’ve been working non-stop since last summer and want to refill our Endurance meter with a small vacation. But we’ll be back in the second half of August to continue our work on the San Rafaela DLC!

And we don’t want to leave you only with this update, so on July 28, this Friday, we’ll announce a contest that will let you not only win a free copy of San Rafaela DLC and get it on release but also will let you be a part of the DLC. Excited? Leave a comment if you are!   

Thank you for your support during this year and through the years of Early Access, Capos. We won’t be able to be here today without your support. We hope that you’ll enjoy the anniversary update and are excited about the San Rafaela DLC (wishlist now)! 

As always, my name is Andrey. If you enjoyed this devlog, join our Discord, follow us on Socials, and leave a like on this video. Have a lovely day, Capos. Bye-bye. 
[/expand]

notes.title: June Update this week!
notes.content:
[h3]Hola Capos! [/h3]

Our [b]June Update is coming this week[/b], and it brings new gameplay mechanics, Balance and UI changes, and bug fixes! We’ve also made some adjustments after our Steam Weekend Playtest, so stick around even if you played it! 

[h2]First off, Gang Alliances! [/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36613041/6176db26fe372065bdf8d8c80ed822340d0e5e9b.gif[/img]
Alliance is a powerful tool that can be used for protection and for strategic advancement. After our Combat Update, we’ve heard you loud and clear that Enemy Gangs could become unreasonably annoying in early and mid-game, so we’ve not only made balance changes but are introducing Gang Alliances that should help with that matter. 

Gang Alliance means that your Allied Gang will stop attacking you, their buildings (including Smuggling Points!) will become available to you, and they even will help you out during Combat! There’s a list of things you need to achieve before being able to strike an Alliance, and you’ll need to keep a close eye on your new friends because, in the world of Cartel Tycoon, they can become enemies really fast. 

After the playtest, we’ve adjusted some things to make achieving an Alliance a bit harder but also made Alliend Gang convoys faster to redeploy. 

[h2]Second, Enforcers vs. Enemy Gangs![/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36613041/5f0d1a13944a0e16f2f71a1ceb045eb00f7cf5ca.gif[/img]
Now Terror affects not only your Cartel but Enemy Gangs too! Enforcers have a chance to attack your enemies instead of you on each trigger of an Attention Star! You can use that to your advantage and capture Enemy buildings while they’re busy with the officials! 

And if the enforcers win the fight - Enemy Gangs will lose power, making it easier for you to make an Alliance or destroy them! 

After the playtest, we’ve made some adjustments to this mechanic and Enemy Gang’s behavior in general! 

[h2]Third, New Gang Agreement UI! [/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36613041/f1d97cd1eeae00bdb10e9ebbc1b7a1c86f38ba02.gif[/img]
Gang Agreements are no longer a dialogue - it’s an easy-to-read menu! 

After the playtest, we’ve made some small adjustments to the menu, so it will be more clear when a new level of Agreement opens to you! 

[h2]Other Changes[/h2]
[b]We’ve reworked how you can attack with weapons![/b] Now, if your lieutenant is in a building that has weapons inside, the game will automatically offer to take weapons if you send them to attack an enemy! It works even when you select multiple LTs! 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36613041/901766eff364aef55b5056289e5f24055b1ca060.gif[/img]

[b]We’ve also expanded the Tutorial![/b] Get ready for more missions that will explain combat and Enemy Gang relations better! 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36613041/837a087a4de5dcacde260bf10dafe59602369fb8.gif[/img]

[b]Global Unlocks Menu is now easier to navigate![/b] Your unlocks will now be in different categories, so you don’t always have to scroll the full list if you want to change a skin for your character! And now you can watch unlocked cinematics again! 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36613041/00b12f71e1fc6d91a30593bb902acd76e126df36.gif[/img]

We’ve made smaller adjustments to new mechanics and squished some nasty bugs! The update is coming soon, and we’ll provide the patch notes with all the changes, as usual! 

[h3]Thank you for participating in the playtest and providing your feedback! ːcartel_loveː

See you soon, Capos!  [/h3]

notes.title: Answering your questions! // Cartel Tycoon Q&A
notes.content:
[h3]Get Cartel Tycoon with 40% off until June 2! [/h3]

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1220140/Cartel_Tycoon/

[h3]___[/h3]

[h3]Hola, Capos! Long time no see ːcartel_loveː

A couple of weeks ago, we gathered your questions, and today we will answer some of them! While we're doing this, the team is hard at work on our next update, which is shaping up to be quite big, and maybe today, we’ll reveal some of the features that are coming… Maybe! 

Let’s get right into it![/h3]

[previewyoutube=MHtcDzcJldk;full][/previewyoutube]

[h3]Prefer the written word? We've got you covered. 
The full transcript is available below:[/h3]

[expand type=details]
There were some repeats from the last Q&As, so I’ll answer those questions briefly at the start! 

[h3]Multiplayer[/h3]

As we said before, with a small team, we have to have priorities, and right now, we want to make Singleplayer the best it can be, so Multiplayer is on the back-burner, and we hope to get back to it at the end of 2023. 

[h3]Mods[/h3]

Same thing with Mods - implementing them into our system is a hefty task that can potentially bring development to a halt, so right now, we’re searching for the best possible way to do it without damaging and derailing our other plans for the game! We saw all of your awesome suggestions for mods. Don’t you worry about that! 

[b]And now, let’s get into other questions![/b]

[b][h3]Q:  Just out of pure curiosity, what's a feature or part of the game that you thought would be simple or straightforward but that turned out to be difficult or confusing to make?[/h3][/b]

I’ve asked around the dev team about that, and I’ve got several different responses! The top two were: Combat Update and Quest-Events. 
Combat Update was pretty minuscule when we first talked about it. We simply wanted to introduce stamina into the game, but it quickly became apparent that this wasn’t going to cut it. So we made a new building, 20+ new abilities, added Weapons, new status effects, and so on and so forth. The design document for the Combat Rework had so many iterations that the end result is completely different from what we envisioned as a small balance change at the start!
And the second feature is Quest-Events. What started as “Hey, let’s create 4-5 events to make the game more interesting” turned into developing a completely new system under the hood with 100+ events inside that adapts to player actions and expansion to make the gameplay more interesting and the world of Cartel Tycoon more lively! 

[b][h3]Q: Are you planning any changes to the combat system in the future? Buffs possibly?[/h3][/b]

If we’re talking about the Combat future as a whole, we currently don’t have big changes planned for the system, but we continue monitoring your feedback and ideas on that matter! On a smaller scale - we’re planning a few balance tweaks to the Endurance and Gang Power across various modes and difficulties. And if we’re talking about the components of the Combat System, like Abilities and Weapons - we have some buffs and changes in the works, and we hope to deliver at least some of the changes with the next update! We’ve got a lot of feedback since the update release, so we now have a more clear picture of what works and what doesn’t from the player’s perspective! 

[b][h3]Q: Are you planning to nerf diplomacy in some way?[/h3][/b]

After the Combat Update, we’ve noticed that many more people are trying to peacefully resolve conflicts with Gangs - by trading with them, talking, and eventually acquiring. Before the Combat Update, that feature was largely overlooked, safe for some insane speedrun strategies and among our more experienced players. Combat Update changed that, and we’ll also be updating our Tutorial to introduce these mechanics better. 

On that note, we don’t want “Diplomacy” to become the go-to strategy, and we want to make both of the routes contextually viable from the early game to the end game, to make either of them make sense in the circumstances because we want players to decide between both of them during their gameplay. So we’re looking at slight balance tweaks that make the peaceful route a bit harder and the combat route a bit more desirable. Jumping into our next question…

[b][h3]Q: Alliances with other gangs are possible soon?[/h3][/b]

I don’t know about “soon,” but it is something that is on our radar! We want to add more ways for players to engage with the world and its characters, so Alliances are something that has come to our mind! We’re working on an initial design, but as you know from question number one - it can be a long road from the design to actual implementation! 

Meanwhile, Alliances aren’t the only new way of engagement we’re thinking about. We’re also playing around with the idea of government forces attacking Enemy Gangs, not just your Cartel. We’re trying out different ways of implementing it and are just thinking if it’s possible to make this cool and exciting without breaking the balance and, you know, the code of the project. We hope that we’ll be able to talk more about it later, but right now, I just wanted to give you a small sneak peek into what types of changes we’re considering for the game!  

[b][h3]Q: What are your plans for survival?[/h3][/b]

Survival Mode is the foundation of Cartel Tycoon as a whole. The development started with it, and everything else came after. But at the same time, the core of Survival Mode hasn’t been changed. Right now, we have several ideas of our own and are consulting with some of our experienced players to find a way of making Survival Mode more engaging. Unfortunately, I can’t tell you more about it, but I can just say that we loved some of the ideas that we were trying for Survival Mode and are going to implement them in a new campaign that will be a part of the San Rafaela expansion! Oh, that reminds me… 

[b][h3]Q: Is the new map coming on the next update?[/h3][/b]

Our new map, San Rafaela, is still being worked on and won’t be a part of the next Cartel Tycoon update. It’s the biggest expansion we’ve ever created for Cartel Tycoon, and it will be available on its own as a DLC. The map isn’t the only part of the DLC - there will be new playable and non-playable characters, a completely new story campaign, and more! We’re aiming to release it during the summer. Before the release, we really want to organize another playtest because we’ve got a lot of very valuable feedback from the first one, and we want to give you all a chance to try out the map completely free close to the release! And we just love sharing work-in-progress stuff with all of you!  Creating a new map is one of our hardest endeavors because we want the gameplay to differ between the two of them, and we want San Rafaela to feel truly special! Be on the lookout for future announcements regarding San Rafaela! We can’t wait to share more with you! 

[b][h3]Q: If you don't release console edition soon I will send the DEA on you so fast!!! Do you have an estimate date for console edition???[/h3][/b]


Whoa-whoa, slow down there, partner! I put my hands where you can see them! The Console edition is moving at a steady pace with the help of some awesome people from tinyBuild! Right now, we expect it to be ready by the Fall of 2023, and we can’t wait to share more on this topic in the future! 
Now, lower your gun, please, and don’t shoot me… 

[b][h3]Q: Do you try to aim for the largest install base for a chance of high profit; or does the platform itself inspire the core design of Cartel Tycoon's idea?[/h3][/b]

I’ll be honest here; me and other devs reread this question multiple times but still have no idea what is being asked. Sooooo…. Yes? Maybe? 

[h3]___[/h3]

I hope that you learned more about the game, about upcoming releases, and a bit about us during this Q&A! 

That’s all for this Q&A session, Capos! If you just thought of an awesome question that you want to be answered - head to our official Discord server! Me and other team members are there every day so that we can answer it there! 
[/expand]

Just to recap and add a bit more context, our plans for this year are as follows.

[b]Summer: [/b]
[list]
[*] A major update
[*] San Rafaela DLC
[/list]
[b]Fall:[/b]
[list]
[*] A major update
[*] Console Release 
[/list]

Of course, some things might move around, and we also might add more updates down the line, but right now, our plans look like this! 

[h3]Have a great day, Capos! More news and announcements are coming! Our next update is coming this summer, and we can’t wait for you to see it! [/h3]

notes.title: Fight & Stash Update // Devlog 25
notes.content:
[h2]Hola Capos![/h2] 

[h3]The first major update of 2023 is almost here, and today I’ll tell you all about what’s inside. Aand when it’s coming out. And when you can enter the playtest to try the update before the release! 

[b]Watch the devlog right now![/b]

[previewyoutube=WpBE0xA9AuU;full][/previewyoutube]

[h3]Prefer the written word? We've got you covered. 
The full transcript is available below:[/h3]

Hola Capos! It’s me, once again. The first major update of 2023 is almost here, and today I’ll tell you all about what’s inside. Aand when it’s coming out. Aaand when you can enter the playtest to try the update before the release. Let’s get right into it. 

[h3][b]I. FIGHT ːcartel_loveː[/b][/h3]

First, let’s talk about the long-awaited rework of combat. The core is still the same - you win if you have more power, no tricks here. But in the new system power is not everything. [b]And if you’re not careful enough - you can lose any fight.[/b] We want combat to be more impactful and require some strategic planning beforehand.

[b]Your Lieutenants are playing a crucial role in the reworked combat[/b]. They can be injured during the fight, they can lose their power, some of them can run away from the battlefield, while others will fight to their dying breath. It’s no longer just about winning the fight with more power points - it’s about building a team with different tactics in mind.

Every Lieutenant now has an Endurance bar which depletes during a fight. The lower it is - the higher the chance to acquire a certain debuff: power loss, injury, or even an arrest. After the fight ends Lieutenants must rest for a bit to refill their Endurance, certain buildings like Residencies or Hotels will speed up this process! 

Power loss and Arrest are pretty self-explanatory but you’re probably wondering how an [b][i]“Injury”[/i][/b] will work. When your Lieutenant is injured during a fight their power no longer counts, so it can be a pretty big blow to your operation! And you also have a choice - you can evacuate your injured Lieutenant from the fight immediately. It will cost some money, of course, but they will be safely recovering in one of your buildings. Or you can decide to leave them on the battlefield. If you win the fight, you’ll still have time to evacuate them. But if you lose… they will die. 

Because Lieutenants are so crucial in the reworked combat system, [b]we made more than 10 new abilities for them and reworked some old ones[/b]. The Coordinator ability is much more useful now! Some of the new abilities are active, some are passive. For example, some of your Lieutenants fight better when they’re alone, and some will make everyone else more powerful. Certain Lieutenants will also acquire buffs to their power instead of debuffs if their Endurance is low. 

We want combat to be much more meaningful and refined, and we want to test it out with all of you before the public release, but that’s not the only thing coming with this update. 

 With a more complex combat system, we’re also introducing a new illegal resource - Weapons. You can’t grow weapons on your farms but you’ll be able to buy them from certain places like Guerillas and Enemy Gangs. Weapons give a boost to your overall power in combat and allow you to perform powerful attacks that can change the tide of the fight. Weapons are optional combat and they are pretty expensive but they can certainly help you out in fights you had no chance of winning without them! 

There are a lot of nuances, a lot of new abilities, and smaller changes that are connected to the Combat Rework. If I listed them all here, this video would’ve been longer than the Godfather trilogy. But I know that all of you are eager to know more and that’s why we’ll be publishing a more detailed guide to the new system in the coming days. And, of course, all of the changes will be listed in the Patch Notes.

But Combat is only half of the update. So let’s get to the second part. 

[h3][b]II. STASH ːcartel_loveː[/b][/h3]

We all know that money can be Dirty or Clean. by the mid-game you can be swimming in Dirty Cash which sounds nice, but also brings a lot of attention to you. Your Selling Points are overflowing, and you’re frantically putting all of your excess Dirty Money in Cities and the Terror is slowly rising. But what if… What if you just hide it? 

”But where” you may ask. And that’s where Caches come in. 

Cache is a new type of building, and its purpose is to let you hide things from the government’s eyes. You can build two types of Caches - Dugouts and Subterreant Storages with different storage sizes which will be useful in different stages of the game or for different purposes. These buildings are hidden and they won’t get attention if you’re not in the process of hiding or taking out the money. 

Feel like a real Capo with hidden caches all around the country! You can hide the excesses for a rainy day when you need to pay a bribe or need some extra cash for laundering buildings. You can, of course, build multiple stashes, and don’t be afraid that some police car will notice them! 

Of course, there’s also a catch - Cartel Tycoon can be a harsh game after all! When your money is hidden in stashes, it will deteriorate over time. There are all kinds of critters underground, so if you forget about your stash for a couple of years you might find an empty storage and a very fat rat. 

We can’t wait for you to check out these buildings and hide dirty money all over your property!

[h3][b]III. PLAYTEST ːcartel_loveː[/b][/h3]

[h3]The playtest of the upcoming update will be starting this week![/h3] We’ll post all of the links on Steam and our Discord! 

We’re still playing around with the sizes of Caches and with new combat mechanics, so during the playtest, we’ll need your help to figure all of this out and release the update with your feedback in mind! 

The update itself is scheduled to release in early April, so we’ll have time to analyze your thoughts and make necessary changes before it hits the stores! 
And the update won’t be the only thing hitting the stores - we’ve created a new Lieutenant Pack with 5 brand-new Lieutenants with abilities related to the new combat system. We’ll make a separate video about them closer to the release of the DLC. 

[h3]------------------[/h3]

[h3]The Fight & Stash Update is the first update we’re releasing this year, but we’ve got a lot more planned for 2023. We hope that you’ll enjoy the changes and new content, and we’re so excited to continue expanding and reforming Cartel Tycoon.[/h3]

[b][h3]See you soon, Capos! Bye-Bye! [/h3][/b]

notes.title: Cartel Tycoon in 2023 // Devlog 24
notes.content:
[h2]Hola Capos![/h2] 

[h3] Today we want to talk about big things coming to Cartel Tycoon in 2023. A new map, a rework of the combat system, and a whole lot more... 

[b]Watch the devlog right now![/b]

And get Cartel Tycoon with a [b]40% discount[/b] until January 30![/h3]

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1220140/Cartel_Tycoon/

[previewyoutube=cbnO_31bS1w;full][/previewyoutube]

[h3]Prefer the written word? We've got you covered. 
The full transcript is available below:[/h3]

Hola Capos! It’s me, Andrey! It’s been a hot minute since you last saw me, and I hope you missed me because I know I missed all of you. Today I would like to talk about our general plans for 2023, our upcoming updates, and the future of Cartel Tycoon. Let’s get into it! 

[h3][b]NEW MAP ːcartel_loveː[/b][/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36613041/e02e702250089b45d45acd4566d90cc25e08f3ff.png[/img]

First off, let’s talk about our [b]general plans for 2023.[/b] We’ve been relatively silent in January, and some of you thought that it meant we abandoned the game and rode off into the sunset. Nope. Reality is much more mundane - we’re working on some big features and we can’t show them yet. For example, [b]another map is one of the biggest things we’ve ever added to the game[/b], and we’re hard at work to show it to you as soon as possible. And because we want to continue developing the game in collaboration with all of you, I can now announce that we’ll launch a public playtest of our next map very soon. 

I don’t want to announce the date yet because the last few years have shown all of us that you can plan ahead all you want, but the world can throw all of your plans under the bus. We’ll get back to this later. 

[h3][b]COMBAT SYSTEM REWORK ːcartel_loveː[/b][/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36613041/496305f8c1ec12cae48551f7773033722d206ab5.png[/img]

As I said in the New Year’s Q&A [b]we’re also working on revamping one of the major Cartel Tycoon systems [/b]that we find underrepresented and a little too simplified and want to make it more exciting and variable. [b]I am talking, of course, about how fights play out in the game.[/b] We don’t want it to simply be “bigger number - better” and are working on a new design that will incorporate a lot more into the equation. For example, we want to make your Lieutenants even more meaningful in fights and are right now experimenting with some of the old abilities and new ones. Right now we’re working out all the kinks of these changes and are looking at how this will work in the game. 

[h3][b]CONSOLE RELEASE ːcartel_loveː[/b][/h3]
Another big thing this year is a [b]console release[/b]. We’re excited for all the Playstation and Xbox players to experience the game. We want all of you to get the best of Cartel Tycoon with whatever device you’re using to play it. At the end of last year, we also added support for [b]GeForce Now[/b], but the game hasn’t appeared as available there yet. But don’t worry - we’re working on it. 

[b](GeForce Now support coming in February!)[/b]

All in all, [b]we have a lot planned for Cartel Tycoon this year[/b], including major updates and expansions to the game. And we will continue making Cartel Tycoon the best it can be. And now back to “plans going under the bus”.

[h3][b]MULTIPLAYER ːcartel_loveː[/b][/h3]
[b]In 2021 we were planning to add multiplayer to Cartel Tycoon[/b]. We know that some of you were patiently and passionately waiting for this feature. Unfortunately, we decided to remove multiplayer from our roadmap [b]for now[/b]. There are a lot of reasons for it, but the bottom line is - we’ve tried a lot of different implementations, and in the end, all of them required a major overhaul of the existing gameplay systems and a lot of time from a small development team. A lot of time. We’ve been on the fence for a long time. We thought: should we focus on a full rewrite of the game to allow the multiplayer or continue expanding the existing single-player experience, making it as fun and polished as it can be? [b]We chose to keep the single player as our main focus for now, as it remains the core of this project. [/b]

[b]That doesn’t mean the multiplayer is completely out of the picture[/b] - we just don’t want to make the same rash decision we made before and announce the date of its arrival.[b] I can just cautiously say that we want to get back to the Co-op Multiplayer at the end of 2023 or in 2024.[/b] Once again, everything might change, and for now, we have removed multiplayer from the roadmap. 

But on the bright side, we’re certain about the future of the Cartel Tycoon and the focus on single-player content will provide a fruitful year! And we can’t wait to show you - not just tell you - what we’ve been cooking up for the upcoming updates.

[h3][b]FIRST UPDATE OF 2023 ːcartel_loveː[/b][/h3]
[b]We’re planning to release the first Cartel Tycoon’s major update of 2023 in February or March[/b], and we’ll do a separate devlog about it closer to its arrival. But I can tell you one cryptic thing now - [i]the Federales can’t find what’s buried underground…[/i] Guess what that means in the comments!  

[h3]------------------[/h3]

[h3]Thank you for sticking with us for all these years, Capos. We’re passionate about Cartel Tycoon, and we think we have a lot more to offer to make the game even bigger and better in the coming months. We hope your 2023 will be great, and we want the time you spent with Cartel Tycoon to be one of the contributing factors. [/h3]

[b][h3]See you very soon, Capos. Goodbye! [/h3][/b]

notes.title: Our plans for 2023 // Cartel Tycoon Q&A (+ Giveaway)
notes.content:
https://store.steampowered.com/app/1220140/Cartel_Tycoon/

[h3][b]Ho-ho-hola Capos! ːcartel_loveː[/b]

The end of the year is approaching fast, and we didn’t want to leave you without a present! So we decided to make this video! We’ll talk about our plans for 2023, answer questions from our Discord community and have a surprise at the end of the video![/h3]

[previewyoutube=hT5v4SX3OHA;full][/previewyoutube]

[h3]Prefer the written word? We've got you covered. 
The full transcript is available below:[/h3]

First things first, let’s talk about 2022. It was a big year for us - with your help we’ve released Cartel Tycoon 1.0 and tons of updates. You helped us so much by …. playtesting, providing feedback, playing the game, leaving reviews both positive…. aaaaand negative. Thank you! 

This year we’ve also been working on many things that are yet to come out, and we’re so excited to bring them to you next year.  Speaking of “next year”… What are our plans for 2023? 

The year is going to be packed - we’re working on the next free content update which will bring a whole new arsenal of things for you to do. And our second map is getting better and better, and we’re almost ready to show you a sneak peek... Oh, we’re ready now? Then let’s show them! The map will feature new ways of transportation, a bigger playing area, new characters, and a whole lot of new regions to explore! We can’t wait for you to try it. 

And the console release is also planned for 2023! We can’t tell when exactly, because there’s still a lot to do, but we’re excited for more people to try out our game. 

The bottom line is - we’ve got a lot planned, and we can’t wait for 2023 to come and for all of you to try out new content! 

[b]But let’s get to the second part of the video - answering your questions![/b] We’ve gathered some questions from our Discord community (by the way, join our Discord), and are ready to answer them! 


[b]Will there be a new and more efficient way to launder cash in the future?[/b]

It’s not a “new” way per se but we’ve got a couple of ideas of new ways with interacting with Dirty Money that won’t lead to Terror rising or buildings getting arrested. I can’t say anything else, guess in the comments!  

[b]What new features are planned for the next major updates? If any? Also, will there be more story quests?[/b]

We’re absolutely going to add more story quests and content. As for the features we’ve got 4 major features that are in different stages of development. Not all of them might make it, but we’re excited to show you what we’re working on next year! 

[b]When is mod support getting added?[/b]

We’re still collecting data and gathering all the ideas for possible mods. It’s not in active development right now, but on our short list of possible features. So continue sharing your mod ideas on Steam and Discord and in the comments to this video!

[b]Will there be weapon dealing in Cartel tycoon and a remake of the power system? [/b]

Well, okay, spoiler alert - one of the designs we’re working on right now - is a revamp of our combat system which includes weapons. It’s rough around the edges and needs some more brain processing to refine it, so it has the right complexity vs smoothness of the experience. We’re constantly thinking about making fights more interesting and will continue working in this direction.

[b]What criteria does the team look at to decide which community feedback is valid and what is not?[/b]

That’s a great and tough question with a long and short answer. We’ll give you both. 
First of all, if something is broken - our QA team makes a bug, and we fix it! 
Secondly, if the player experience is different from what we have imagined - we go back to the drawing board to find ways to fix it. 
And If the feedback is regarding a system we ourselves want to change or improve - we take it into the consideration when redesigning this aspect of the game, which might take a long time, but it doesn’t mean that the feedback is forgotten! 
And the short answer is - it all depends on how many available resources we have to implement your ideas into the game. When you’re a small development team you have to prioritize some things. If we could implement all of your awesome suggestions - we would, but sometimes even a small change from the players' perspective takes a lot of time to implement and requires a lot of work from the whole team, so, unfortunately, it doesn’t get into the game. 

Turns out it was two long answers, but I hope we were able to give perspective you understand! It’s no secret now that we’re gearing up for our next project, and we learned (and continue to learn) a lot from Cartel Tycoon, including your feedback. 

[b]How did the focus on drugs come into the team? Was it a core idea for the lore or an afterthought? Was the separation of both cash (clean and dirty) a cause or a consequence?[/b]

Well, in the early stages we were inspired by “Breaking Bad” and wanted to make an experience focused on struggling with maintaining an ever-growing criminal empire. But we decided to focus on the bigger theme so we would have more narrative and design choices. At that stage, we were thinking about the game as the complete opposite of Ghost Recon: Wildlands, where you would play as an antagonist. So the drugs were here from the beginning.
The separation of money into Clean and Dirty was inspired by the story of how Pablo Escobar got caught and was added to the game in the first months of development. 

But the structure and economics of the game were inspired by the great book called “Narconomics” which studies the bureaucracy of the drug empires 

[b]Why an unspecified country in Central America?[/b]

Cartel Tycoon takes inspiration from a lot of places, so we felt that sticking to a real country would close up a lot of opportunities in stories and game mechanics and we didn’t want the game to be “realistic” per se. That’s why we distance ourselves from real places and real people and want to focus on the player experience, and not the specific story of a specific location! 

[h3]_________________[/h3]

Whew, hope you liked it! We want to do these kinds of Q&A’s semi-regularly, so if you’re interested - tell us in the comments below! 

And now for the giveaway. Holidays are approaching fast, so we wanted to give something away to a couple of lucky people from our community! And what’s better than a huge-$*@ Cartel Tycoon-themed mouse pad? Enter our giveaway on gleam.io (the link is in the description) and win a mouse pad of your choosing, and we’ll send it.. uhhh, I mean Santa will send it to you. 

[h2][url=https://gleam.io/myfmE/cartel-tycoon-mousepad-giveaway]JOIN THE GIVEAWAY HERE![/url][/h2]

[h3]Happy holidays, Capos! See you in 2023! [/h3]

notes.title: Sacred Lamb Update // Devlog 23
notes.content:
[h2]Hola Capos![/h2] 

[h3]“The Sacred Lamb” Update brings you more end-game content, multiple quality-of-life changes, and bug fixes! Learn more about the upcoming update in this devlog! [/h3]

[previewyoutube=A4vTSsjvveY;full][/previewyoutube]

[h3]Prefer the written word? We've got you covered. 
The full transcript is available below:[/h3]

Hola Capos! It’s Andrey! It’s been a month since the Goals & Gains Update, and we’re here to bring you another one! “The Sacred Lamb” Update brings you more end-game content, multiple quality-of-life changes, and many-many bug fixes. Let’s get right into it!

Huh, just joking! Don’t forget to like, subscribe and leave comments down below! My Lieutenants are watching you do it. All done? Good, let’s get one with the devlog! 

We’ll start with Special Buildings. “Why?” you may ask. They’re an essential part of the new end-game content coming with the update. In order to access it you’ll need to capture all of the Special Buildings, and a new questline will open to you. If you decide to pursue it, you’ll meet new characters, make tough decisions and acquire desirable unlocks. This questline will test you but believe me, it will be worth it. 

As always, your choices will matter and will lead to different endings, but you’ll be satisfied either way! 

We’ve also updated our Lieutenant List. It’s no longer a Lieutenant list, but a Character List - navigate to your favorite Mayors, Gang Leader-buddies, and, of course, Lieutenants with one menu! No more running your mouse through all of your cities looking for that one Mayor that didn’t give you a loan yet - just find them through the menu!

With this update, we’re also bringing a new type of Lieutenant Ability - the one you can toggle on or off, which gives you more wiggle room and creative ways to use your lieutenants. We want you to feel more in control of your Cartel, and we’ll continue to fight… I mean work in this direction.

And speaking of control, we’re bringing more Advanced Settings to the Sandbox Mode. You’ll be able to control the Events and the Market. You’ll be able to turn them off completely if you so desire, and you’ll be able to control the frequency of the Events and the Market “Difficulty”. Make the Sandbox truly special for yourself! 

We’re also adding the search bar to the Research Tree! Find the desired building or an upgrade in seconds! You loved the Research Queue addition in the last update, so we’re making the Research Tree even more accessible with this update. 

We’re also giving some love to those of you who bought the game called “Cartel Tycoon” but still want a family-friendly endeavor. Your legal packages with nothing illegal inside will no longer draw suspicion from the government which will make building a legal empire an easier task for you! 

And, of course, there will be lots of smaller quality-of-life changes and bug fixes, some of which we spotted ourselves, and some of which you reported on our forums! Thank you for that! 

The Sacred Lamb Update is coming very soon, and we can’t wait for you to check it out! 

Thanks for watching! Subscribe to our socials, and join Discord to chat with the devs and fans and enjoy some exclusive content. See you, Capos!

notes.title: Goals & Gains Update // Devlog + Patch Notes
notes.content:
[h2]Hola Capos![/h2] 

[h3]Our next update - [b]Goals & Gains[/b] is here, so it’s time for you to know what’s inside. Let’s get right into it! 

And now is the perfect time to get Cartel Tycoon with a [b]30% discount[/b]![/h3]

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1220140/Cartel_Tycoon/

[previewyoutube=krtH5pdl7E8;full][/previewyoutube]

[h3]Devlog script: [/h3]
[expand type=details]Hola Capos! It’s me - Andrey! I haven’t seen you since the 1.0 Release, so it’s good to be back with another devlog! And it’s a big one. Our next update - Goals & Gains is coming very soon, so it’s time for you to know what’s inside. Let’s get right into it! 


[b]Global Goals.[/b] We’ve been hinting about this addition on our socials, and some of you might’ve already figured it out! We’re adding Global Goals to Sandbox Mode - you can choose or simply play without them, but completing a Global Goal will grant you unique goodies - special character skins, for example! 
Global Goals differ and you can decide on how to approach them! And if you fail them - don’t worry, you can keep playing your Sandbox game and try again later!


[b]The Logistics.[/b] When the game hit 1.0, we got a lot of new players and feedback about the logistics part of the game. So we’ve been working on improving it since the release. There are a lot of changes under the hood but with the new system in place, there no longer should be a situation when one of your Workshops is loaded with products and the other ones sit empty. We’ve also adjusted how Residencies distribute Dirty Money between production and city buildings! 

[b]New Events.[/b] With this update, we’re also adding new events that can happen in your game! For example, Building Events that can affect your production, adding more variety to the process. Also, we’re adding Enemy Gang Events - some of which will require a hard choice to make but will spice up your interactions with Gang Leaders and introduce players to some Gang Mechanics they weren’t using before. Did you already know that you can talk to the Gang Leader to better your relationship? With new Gang Events, you certainly will! 

[b]Saving and Loading times.[/b] With the 1.0 Release, a lot of you pointed out that the game sometimes takes too long to save. Since the release, we’ve been optimizing and rewriting the system, so now your games should load and save much faster, and the size of your saves got reduced significantly! We’ll continue monitoring your feedback on this so we can further improve the system but our internal tests look promising! 

[b]Research Tree.[/b] Research Tree also got lots of love in this update - now the game will remember where you were on the Research Tree when you closed it, so you don’t have to find Warehouse III when you open it again. And that’s not all! You can now….. DRUMROLL PLEASE…. Queue research! Yep, you heard me right! Add everything you want to Research to the Queue, pay upfront - and if you changed your mind about Warehouse - just delete it from the queue and get the money back! 

We’ve also made a lot of small visual changes, fixed a lot of bugs, and generally had an awesome time reading all of your feedback and finding ways to implement it into the game. We want to thank everyone who supported our game from the start and those of you who joined us with the 1.0. We’re grateful that you gave Cartel Tycoon a shot, and we want to make the game even better for all of you! 

I know, I know, cut down on the sentimentalities, you’re here to learn about the update and when it’s coming. So here it is...

The Goals & Gains is coming out... TODAY! Go to the stores and update the game! 

Thanks for watching, don’t forget to like and subscribe and also leave your comments down below. Subscribe to our socials, and join Discord to chat with the devs, and fans of the game and enjoy some exclusive content. See you, Capos! 
[/expand]

[h2]Cartel Tycoon v.1.0.9.4445 Patch Notes[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36613041/4163dfdd0c3b158da58fff33516fc45ed93a4d7d.png[/img]

[h3]Major changes[/h3]

ːcartel_loveː [b]Global Goals![/b] We’re adding 4 end-game missions to Sandbox! Just playing around can be fun, but having a goal in mind can be even more fun! You can choose your own Global Goal when starting a new Sandbox Game, and if you complete it - you’ll get a special reward! It’s Sandbox, so you can choose your own way to approach this goal! [b]Global Goals Unlocks[/b] can be obtained only on standard Sandbox Settings (easy, medium, and hard) 
ːcartel_loveː [b]Logistics reworked! [/b] We’ve made significant changes to the internal prioritization systems, so your money and your products would be delivered to their destinations much more smoothly, and situations, where one of your buildings stays completely empty while the other is overflowing with produce, won't be happening. We've also remade priorities for Residencies, so the Residence doesn't deliver all the money to laundering buildings without leaving anything for the production chain upkeep. 
ːcartel_loveː [b]Save System optimized![/b] We’ve been doing a lot of optimizations under the hood and updating how our saving system works. We managed to shrink the file size for saves 20x! The saving process itself is 10 times faster, and loading times tripled in speed. When you start your game for the first time, it could take some time to optimize your old saves but it should be smooth sailing after this!
ːcartel_loveː [b]Research Queue added![/b] Add everything you want to Research to the Queue, pay upfront, and if you changed your mind about something - just delete it from the queue and get the money back! 
ːcartel_loveː [b]New Events![/b] We’re introducing new Events for buildings and Enemy Gangs! It means more interactions with Enemy Gangs and it means keeping an eye out on your production and logistics systems! 
ːcartel_loveː [b]Heroin changed![/b] We heard that Heroin wasn’t as satisfying to produce, so we changed the amount of product that is needed to make it! We've also made adjustments to its Market fluctuations. These changes will make this drug MUCH more desirable to produce!
ːcartel_loveː [b]Airport balance changed! [/b] We've lowered the time needed to sell a batch of products, so your Lieutenants can be available at a faster rate while still selling the same amount of produce, which will make it a more desirable Special Building to control!

[*] Added a loading screen before the Main Menu appears when you start the game. It also loads much faster!
[*] Terror Scale now appears at the start of the "Needs and Fears" campaign.

notes.title: Contest Results + Small Development Update
notes.content:
[h3]Hola Capos! 

Last week we announced the winners of our Sandbox Stories contest on Discord! Check out their stories and Sandbox Settings below! [/h3]

ːcartel_loveː [url=https://discord.com/channels/716885412467048539/857337640286421013/1009470564588593255]Gentlemen of Los Grandes[/url] by MinaBlack 
[expand type=details] The Los Caballeros de los Grandes cartel originally assembled as a ring of kidnappers known as "Los Arañas" (The Spiders) was described having a higher social background than most other traffickers of the time. The group were implicated in numerous kidnappings and use the profits to fund their drug trafficking empire. The assembled group first involved itself in trafficking marijuana. Due to the product's low profit rate and large amounts required to traffic to cover resources, the fledgling group decided to shift their focus to a more lucrative drug, cocaine. In order to launder the incoming money of the trafficking operations, the cartel heavily invested its funds into legitimate business ventures like banks, as well as front companies to mask the money. Their goal is to control the world's marijuana and cocaine market and build a $7 billion a year criminal enterprise.

Early game:
- Start in Los Grandes region
- Choose a starting capo with kidnapping ability
- Hire lieutenants with kidnapping ability only (even the ability is not yet activated)
- Spend the starting dirty and legal money for anything except building illegal businesses.
- Collect $70,000 thru kidnapping (starting legal money not included)
- Once you collected the money, you can start building illegal businesses.

But today we have a [b]minor update[/b] with some of the changes you asked for! And bug fixes, of course (more of those coming next week). We [b]rebalanced up Events from Lieutenants[/b], [b]updated the Transport Company interface[/b], and [b]added the ability to stop Lieutenants when they’re moving[/b]. notes.title: Tycoon or Survival?
notes.content:
[h3]Back in 2019, we were brainstorming the name of the game. One of the proposed variants caught our attention immediately - Cartel Tycoon. Catchy and Self-explanatory, right? Yes, but…[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36613041/287d987b78589d02b47aed6488934c49988ef663.png[/img]

As we've found out later on, for some of you, it was somewhat misleading, as the Tycoon genre is so broad and versatile. Our primary inspiration sources were Tropico and Frostpunk, not exactly Tycoons, more like Survival games. 

[h3]So let's find out, are we more Tycoon than Survival or vice versa?[/h3]

[b]Tycoon:[/b] Build your production chains

[b]Survival:[/b] But… Production requires periodic tweaking and micromanagement, and Buildings can and will be seized, burned, or destroyed

You, as a young and naive Capo, start small and plan a grand success for your Cartel. At first, all goes well; money starts to flow in. And here problems begin! Government starts to notice you and enemy gangs as well. And at this moment, you know… real Cartel started its journey.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36613041/32f3794a868fe4974c096483c816ce7c10652bb9.png[/img]

[b]Tycoon:[/b] Generate resources and profit

[b]Survival:[/b] But…Lose it due to federals confiscating your warehouses and residences as there is no silver bullet to avoid all the negative events

Time passes, and you expand your empire, but there's always this struggle - how to get rid of all these excess resources and dirty money piled up all around your residence, warehouses, and smuggling points?

Expand! You expand, build more, and now all looks good, but not for long, as now you have even more money you need to deal with! Hyperprofit that's one of your enemies in our game. Maybe it's time to burn the excess, but we don't have a crematorium in-game 😃
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36613041/a235645ef29fc21e35615442ee2d3310812ca058.png[/img]

[b]Tycoon:[/b] Personnel management

[b]Survival:[/b] But…Deal with all their needs, meltdowns and personal quests, and greed for money, of course

New lieutenants - loyal, working for free cause they idolize you. They grow, become powerful, and at the same time, greedy. And you, as a leader, harsh but fair, decide how to deal with those who want to dethrone you. Maybe it's a jail that will cool them off, or some accident with a gas stove will get rid of them, who knows. Or maybe… money, money can solve many problems but not all of them.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36613041/65f3e4e7de8a6c6886881be774c44c09b100cb09.png[/img]


[b]Tycoon:[/b] Do business with the competitors (Enemy Gangs)

[b]Survival:[/b] But… Fend off their constant attacks while trying to lower a Terror

The whole world is against you, there are no friends to rely on. You're alone. And the burden of responsibility grows with every new farm, every new region. You fight your way with everything you have: Bribes, Takeovers, Assassinations, Wars against enemy gangs, and government with their infinite law enforcement capabilities.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36613041/ebf9191e05a8c7eda04ffbbb5157dfe9111ada49.png[/img]


[h3]That's the experience we're trying to share with you, show you the other side - Building your empire against all the odds and challenges the world throws at you. By the way, "Narconomics" by Tom Wainwright was one of the inspiration materials for Cartel Tycoon.[/h3]

[h3]And our main goal and challenge are to present this experience as enjoyable to you, our players as possible, so [b]we continue to add QoL, balance changes, and fixes to the game for a better experience with every update.[/b]

We hope you enjoyed this little reflection on the topic.[/h3]

[h2]Are we Tycoon or Survival? or something else…

Please Let us know in the comments what you think. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36613041/fb508f39ffb60ef5b007e6052e8b1016e8eb6cb7.png[/img]

Show 'em what you're worth, Capo! ːcartel_nothing_personalː[/h2]

notes.title: Steam Publisher Sale + Pricing news
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36613041/345eacf92b65f64045ecb0cd00b17d103bf9629a.png[/img]

[h3]Hola, Capos ːcartel_loveː[/h3]

[b]Last week we left Early Access.[/b] We’ve been working non-stop to make our 1.0 Release as packed as it can be - some of the features like Enemy Gangs and Special Buildings were beta-tested out by all of you on Steam, but we packed the release with lots of other additions and reworks.

[b]Since the 1.0 Release, we’ve made 2 patches, and aim to deliver the third one next week[/b]. We’ve also got a lot of feedback, and are already working on ways we can improve the player experience in Cartel Tycoon further, and we aim to release these changes along with new content in September.  

With the 1.0 Release comes [i]a slight price increases [/i] for the game that, of course, won’t affect those who already got the game during its' Early Access phase. The game now is twice as big as it was the last year, and we don’t only mean the file size. 

[b]Since starting in EA, we’ve made a new campaign, completely reworked Sandbox and Survival, made a Tutorial, a myriad of changes to the game, and a whole lot of additions[/b]. 

We want to provide even more, and [b]we already have plans for the upcoming FREE content updates, one of which is coming out this September along with a roadmap for our future plans![/b]

[b]The game will be priced at [i]29.99$[/i] starting from [u]August 12[/u][/b], and the regional price will be adjusted to reflect this change. The prices will change after the tinyBuild sale ends on August 12, so [b]now you have a perfect opportunity to buy Cartel Tycoon 1.0 not only for the Early Access price but with a 30% sale discount! [/b]

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1220140/Cartel_Tycoon/

We’re so excited to watch the vision for Cartel Tycoon that we have crafted come to life during and after the Early Access period. [b]“We” means both us and you, the players, because you helped so much.[/b] We once again want to thank you for your support and assure you that the game will be becoming better and larger (again, not just the file size) with every upcoming update. 

[h3]- Moon Moose[/h3]

notes.title: Hotfix and our plans for the Logistics system!

notes.title: Cartel Tycoon 1.0 is LIVE!
notes.content:
[h2]Hola Capos!

Cartel Tycoon 1.0 is here! Download the latest patch and enjoy the full release! [/h2]

[h3]Watch the gameplay trailer now![/h3]

[previewyoutube=qcGe052L2xw;full][/previewyoutube]

[h2]PATCH NOTES: [/h2]

ːcartel_sadː [b]Your old saves won't work with this update[/b]

[h3]Major changes[/h3]

ːcartel_loveː [b]Special Buildings[/b] are in the game: Prison, Airport, Indigenous Territory, Guerillas, and Military Base have been activated, and now you can use them! Each Building introduces new quests, new mechanics, and unique characters!

ːcartel_loveː [b]Loyalty Scale Rework[/b]: Bonuses added to Loyalty Scale. Loyalty now lowers with time; if it reaches zero - your Capo will die! Each playthrough starts with a positive Loyalty level.

ːcartel_loveː [b]Unique Mayor Quests[/b]: Each city now has a pool of unique quests.

ːcartel_loveː [b]Global Unlocks Rework[/b]: Now any Lieutenant that becomes a Capo in your game will become a Starting Capo. But some still have unique quests! We’ve also changed unlock conditions for Collectors Residence and River Pier upgrades! 

ːcartel_loveː [b]Multiple changes to the region visuals[/b]. Now Neutral and Enemy Regions have different colors and look prettier than ever.

ːcartel_loveː [b]Enemy Gangs[/b]. Each gang has a leader. You can talk to leaders, make agreements to buy or sell products and safely transport Dirty Money through their cities without giving them a cut. Enemy Gangs will react to players' actions across the regions. Players will have multiple ways of defeating a gang.

ːcartel_loveː [b]New Resources[/b]: Dried Opium, Sauce, Quinoa, Avocado, Dog Food.

ːcartel_loveː [b]New Illegal Resource[/b] - Heroin. It’s an end-game drug made from Dried Opium.

ːcartel_loveː [b]New Building - Food Factory.[/b]

ːcartel_loveː [b]Added Quest Panel[/b]. You can now pin quests or hide them from the screen.

ːcartel_loveː [b]Updated Research[/b]. Research Center renamed to University. You can Research Tiers I and II without a University. University is required to research Tier III buildings.

ːcartel_loveː You can now [b]reroll Lieutenants[/b] available for recruitment.

ːcartel_loveː [b]Resource Finder[/b] that helps to quickly locate and visualize resources and dirty money in your buildings.

ːcartel_loveː Added [b]19 achievements[/b], collect 'em all!

ːcartel_loveː Added [b]28 new music tracks[/b]

ːcartel_loveː [b]Fully voiced tutorial objectives and dialogues[/b] [i](English only)[/i]

ːcartel_loveː [b]Steam Cloud Saves[/b]

notes.title: Cartel Tycoon 1.0 // Devlog 21
notes.content:
[h2]Hola Capos![/h2] 

[h3]Tons of new features,  hundreds of Quality of Life changes, and reworks are packed in Cartel Tycoon 1.0! Learn more about them in this devlog! [/h3]

[previewyoutube=AWnCz4aMg0w;full][/previewyoutube]

[h3]Prefer the written word? We've got you covered. 
The full transcript is available below:[/h3]

July 26  is right around the corner. This is it, huh? After 3 years of development, we have finally reached the full release of Cartel Tycoon. Well, almost. Once again, my name is Andrey, and I’m the community manager of Cartel Tycoon. Welcome to Devlog 21, and welcome to Cartel Tycoon 1.0. Let’s begin. 

Today I will tell you all about what’s coming to Cartel Tycoon with the 1.0 Release. There’s a lot to cover so let’s get down to business. But if you want to take a trip down memory lane first - you can find the post titled “Road from Early Access to 1.0” on all our socials.


1.0 Release is full of new features - some of them our community on Discord has been testing since Spring, and some of them will be new for everyone. First of all, fully functioning Special Buildings with lots of unique features - Prison, Airport, Military Base, Guerilla Camp, and Indigenous Territory are in the game. They’ve been developed with your needs, feedback, and wants in mind, and they are useful from the early game to the end game, changing the balance of the regions quite drastically. If you want to know more about them - check out this Devlog right here. 

[previewyoutube=XuNcieCfP7Y;full][/previewyoutube]

Another feature that changes the balance are Enemy Gangs.  They know have faces, needs, fears, and personalities, and their actions are affected by yours. We have a special devlog about Gangs too, check it out right here. 

[previewyoutube=jutkPIAF3Ts;full][/previewyoutube]

A new drug is also coming to the game - Heroin. It’s one of the most difficult to produce, but it also brings the most money. The introduction of heroin overhauls the end game and gives a new purpose to the starting drug - Opium, which wasn’t very useful after the first few hours of the gameplay before. Along with a new illegal product, we’re bringing two new legal ones that you can grow - Avocado and Quinoa, which are quite expensive on their own - new contenders for your family-friendly empire, but also offer more variety in packaging for your sneaky needs! 


Also, we’re introducing a new building called the Food Factory - it can produce dog food and sauces, so now you have another option of producing legal products - not only growing or buying! 


As for more QoL changes, we’ve made a new filter called “Resource Finder” - you can use it to check what product is located where on a grand scale. This feature will help locate not only products but Dirty Money too - no more searching through your property for cash - just click a button and see where it is!


We’ve also got another major rework - Global Unlocks. We’ve been tweaking the system for a while now, to make the process more natural, reworking the objectives players needed to complete. But there was still a major problem - River Piers. Completing the “That Sinking Feeling” campaign and getting that sweet-sweet [REDACTED] as a reward is pretty good, but locking players out of the upgrades if they don’t want to play Story Mode - is not. River Pier upgrades will be open to everyone, but those who complete the campaign will still get that sweet-sweet [REDACTED], as a skin for River Pier III.


Another important feature coming with 1.0 is Steam Cloud Saves! Yay, now you don’t have to keep your save files on you every time you want to play Cartel Tycoon away from your PC - they’re in the clouds now! 


Also, our awesome artists from around the globe have been working on the new OST for the game! We’ve got lots of new songs from the artists we’ve worked with in Early Access, and from the new ones - who joined us in the Full Release. For example, this song right now!

And, of course, what’s a full release of the game without achievements! We’ve got easy ones, we’ve got hard ones, we’ve got funny ones - we’ve got them all. Completionists, rejoice! You now can 100% Cartel Tycoon! 


As always, we’ve got a lot of smaller changes we’ll be bringing to the game. For example, we’ve improved our transportation logic a bit, so your trucks will be using their full potential when delivering goods! Many more changes are coming, and we’ll share them in the Patch Notes! 


We also wanted to thank those of you, who’ve been with us since the Early Access, so if you own Cartel Tycoon already, you’ll be getting special cartel emblems to use in-game. Everyone who got the game in Early Access and made their tinyBuild account will get them, so if you don’t have the game yet, you can get them too if you purchase the game before the 1.0 hits! 


All of us in Moon Moose would like to, once again, thank all of you for being on this journey with us. Cartel Tycoon wouldn’t be what it is today without your feedback, thoughts, and suggestions.


Cartel Tycoon releases on July 26, and we’re so happy to finally be here. But the work doesn’t stop - we’re working on optimizing the game, making it even more beautiful and polished to provide you with the 1.0 Release we can truly call 1.0! 

We’re Moon Moose and we thank you for believing in us. See you on July 26, Capos. Goodbye.
